items.title: Nodusfall Accused of Being an Elden Ring Rip-Off
Genshin Impact devs' new action game Nodusfall feels like Elden Ring Nightreign at home, but don't write it off yet
items.summary: Going hands-on with Nodusfall at Gamescom 2026
items.content:
Going hands-on with Nodusfall at Gamescom 2026

(Image credit: HoYoverse) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Facebook X Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Nodusfall does not look like your typical Hoyoverse game. Distinctly lacking in bright colors and bubbly anime-style characters, it's hard to believe that this gloomy, intense PvE action game comes from the same studio behind Genshin Impact and Honkai: Star Rail. But after a brief hands-on session with the game, I'm already eager to dive back in for more.

It might not look like a Hoyoverse game, but there's one thing Nodusfall certainly does look like. Namely Elden Ring , and by extension, its co-op sibling Nightreign . This doesn't end with its reveal trailer vibes – we have a summonable Torrent-like steed who can be called with a very familiar-sounding whistle, a character who can transform into a phase two Malenia lookalike with massive, crusty wings, Estus flask-like healing potions, and bonfires to rest at.

Developer: MiHoYo Platfom(s): PC Release date: TBC

Needless to say, it's hard not to draw comparisons – 'we've got Elden Ring Nightreign at home,' my brain screams. However, while teaming up with other players to take down big bosses might evoke feelings of FromSoftware 's co-op title, there's a big difference with Nodusfall: it's not nearly as hard. This can be considered a blessing or a curse depending on where you stand on Soulslike difficulty. As a fan of the genre, I still found myself having plenty of fun taking down the three bosses in my hands-on session, including an enormous dragon and Qiongqi (a horned and winged tiger-like beast from Chinese mythology), but my victories definitely didn't come with the same level of satisfaction as they might have had they been slightly harder won. I can't recall falling in battle even once, largely thanks to what felt like an unlimited supply of heals.

To be fair, this factor may also have been helped by one of the playable characters being a dedicated healer, who I choose to play in my session. I have strong magic attacks up my sleeve, from small projectiles to ice-powered strikes and an enormous laser beam move, but my main contribution to my team comes in the form of my healing abilities. I can choose to lock onto a specific ally to unleash a steady flow of health restoration, not unlike Mercy's Caduceus staff in Overwatch, or heal multiple teammates around me at once in a smaller burst.

The specific ally lock-on heal can feel a little clunky at times – there were more than a few times where I assisted someone who definitely didn't need it because they were awkwardly stood in front of someone else who desperately needed my help. Comparing directly to Elden Ring Nightreign, though, it's really cool to have a healer option in the first place. Again, it seems that Nodusfall doesn't come close to being as challenging as FromSoftware's Soulslikes to begin with, but having a medic role like this is no doubt going to provide a welcome option to players who aren't as comfortable with getting up close and personal on the frontlines of a brutal battle. I always tend to gravitate towards support classes in games – there's just something so satisfying about keeping your friends and allies going – so I'm pleased to be allowed that here.

Nodusfall looks more like Monster Hunter and Elden Ring than games from Genshin Impact's Hoyoverse Nodusfall isn't a gacha game, Mihoyo confirms Mihoyo CEO says Monster Hunter-like Nodusfall is very "un-Mihoyo," which hopefully means less gacha I'd have been curious to try out the other playable characters to get a greater feel for Nodusfall's combat. What I experienced was fun, but my attacks felt like they were lacking weight, leaving me craving just a tad more oomph. You really can't fault the boss battles when it comes to how cinematic they are, though – my team and I tore through multiple phases in each fight, with our final battle against the Maldrake dragon evolving after the knight riding on its back dismounted their steed and began attacking us from the ground, forcing us to split our forces to take on two enemies at once.

The concept of an easier, more accessible co-op action game like Nightreign is bound to be appealing

Though my Nodusfall experience was limited to co-op PvE, Hoyoverse has clarified that PvP and PvPvE modes are also planned for the long term, and that you'll also be able to enjoy most of the core content solo. From what I played, though, it'd be a shame to do so since you'd miss out on the flashy Joint Execution moves – who doesn't want to team up to drive a massive greatsword through a beast's head?

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

I was also pleased to learn that, despite plans to make Nodusfall a free-to-play game, playable characters won't be locked behind a gacha system. With that said, the devs are considering monetizing cosmetics, and I can't say I'm surprised. While kitting out my healer girl with a new outfit, various accessories including a fancy, glowing cape were screaming microtransaction potential. I can't say I love that aspect, but I'd certainly much rather the monetization be incorporated here than the core gameplay.

As someone who loved Elden Ring Nightreign, I suppose it's only natural that I'd enjoy Nodusfall. Its vibe is very similar, but I'm very curious to see where Hoyoverse takes it from here. The concept of an easier, more accessible co-op action game like Nightreign is bound to be appealing to many, and could be a bridge for those who find FromSoftware's games a bit too difficult. Regardless, there's something in here that's got me craving more – but for now, I guess I've literally got Nightreign at home.

items.title: Elden Ring Tarnished Edition Review Roundup: Strongly Recommended Despite Technical Flaws
items.summary: Elden Ring Tarnished Edition review roundup: critics call the Switch 2 port a triumph, with 100% recommending it despite technical compromises.
items.content:
Gaming Elden Ring Tarnished Edition Review Roundup: Strongly Recommended Despite Technical Flaws GameDaily Follow Franz Christian Irorita Tue, September 1, 2026 at 10:30 PM UTC Tue, September 1, 2026 at 10:30 PM UTC Elden Ring Tarnished Edition Review Roundup: Strongly Recommended Despite Technical Flaws Elden Ring Tarnished Edition has landed, and the verdict is close to unanimous. FromSoftware's Nintendo Switch 2 port sits at 90 on Metacritic with a Must-Play badge and 89 on OpenCritic, where it holds a "Mighty" rating, ranks in the top 2% of games on the site, and is recommended by 100% of critics.

OpenCritic: 89 – Mighty, 100% of critics recommend

Critics all agree that Elden Ring Tarnished Edition is a recommendation just waiting to happen. Not a single one of the 45 critic reviews counted by Metacritic landed as mixed or negative, which is a genuinely rare outcome for a port of this technical ambition.

Nintendo Life called it "a tremendous achievement and one of the finest games you can currently play" on the platform, crediting the density of its open world and the fact that it delivers a full DLC endgame expansion alongside the base game.

DualShockers went further, framing the entire evaluation around one question, how does it run, and concluding it's "one of, if not the, best third-party games on the Nintendo Switch 2."

GamingBolt set price concerns aside to call it "one of the best games of this generation, if not of all time," while Digitally Downloaded argued that any gap between this version and the PlayStation 5 release amounts to a rounding error, summing up its stance on the compromises involved.

The package itself is a significant part of the appeal. It bundles the base game with the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion, adds two new classes, plus a Tarnished Pack adding new weapons and Torrent armor skins. Multiple reviews singled out the two new starting classes as a reason for returning players to begin a fresh run rather than treating this purely as a portability play, giving many players the excuse to jump into The Lands Between all over again.

Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition is getting recommended by critics despite its technical compromises, although the game's state now has come a long way since it was first unveiled to the public.

TheSixthAxis drew the sharpest line between audiences, arguing that newcomers will find the magic fully intact while, for anyone who has played elsewhere, "the performance downgrades may be too much to take."

INVEN was blunter about the specific cost, noting the port pushes past the hardware's limits but that "its relatively low frame rate can be a constant burden" for a game built on precise, reactive combat, with quirks like returning to the menu after sleep mode undercutting portable play.

Gaming Age , at the low end of the range, said it's "still a great game, warts and all" while recommending anyone with more powerful hardware play it elsewhere.

Several outlets also flagged the absence of cross-save as a real missed opportunity, and French outlet Gameblog pointed specifically to frame rate drops making certain sequences harder to read in handheld mode.

Users, however, aren't as forgiving for the game's technical flaws as the critics have been.

Metacritic's user score sits at 7.8 from 58 ratings, with 21% of those ratings landing negative. That's a wider spread of user opinion than the unanimous critic response suggests, and it reflects the split TheSixthAxis identified between newcomers and players comparing against other platforms.

items.summary: Nintendo has released an official guide for beginners playing Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition on Switch 2, introducing newcomers to the basics of traversing the Lands Between.
items.content:
1 Источник: YouTube-канал Nintendo of America 30 August 2026, 11:15 Dmitry Krivov Nintendo has released an official guide for beginners playing Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition on Switch 2, introducing newcomers to the basics of traversing the Lands Between.

The release of Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition on Nintendo Switch 2 took place on August 28, 2026. For this event, Nintendo and Bandai Namco prepared a short video with basic tips for those new to a FromSoftware game. The guide explains the core principles of Elden Ring and tells what to expect during the journey through the Lands Between. The player's main goal is to explore the world, collect the shards of the shattered Elden Ring, and ultimately become the Elden Lord.

Tarnished Edition includes the main game and the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion. The edition also received new content: starting classes Idus Knight and Heavy Knight, new weapons and equipment, and the ability to change Torrent's appearance. Some of the content is available to owners of the game on other platforms via the paid Tarnished Pack.

Initial reviews indicate that the Switch 2 version turned out technically much better than early demonstrations showed.

items.title: I Tested Elden Ring On Switch 2 In A Cozy Cafe And It Ran Just Fine, Which Is Great News For A Remarkable Game
items.summary: You shouldn't play it in the rain/but you can play it on a train
items.content:
Elden Ring is an excellent, excellent video game. It’s got that smashy FromSoftware combat, a couple hundred boss fights that are all (mostly) unique and fun, character build customization for miles, a gorgeous and massive open world that’s a treat to explore, an intriguing story and hidden secrets, and a robust DLC that could be a game all its own. There’s a reason (well, many reasons!) why it’s almost universally critically acclaimed and still beloved by fans a few years after launch, too.

I love Elden Ring ! But when Ethan asked me to take on the review of the Tarnished Edition on Nintendo Switch 2, I wasn’t, like, stoked about it. I beat Elden Ring back when it first came out, easily dumping over 100 hours into the main game and probably another solid 40 or more into the DLC. And I played the Tarnished Edition at a preview event earlier this year for about 20 minutes, after which time I told everyone I spoke with about the experience that yup, that was Elden Ring all right! Elden Ring on a Switch 2! Game’s great, but I don’t necessarily need to play it again. What else is there to say?

It turns out, after playing for review, I do have one additional thing to say: Elden Ring is, apparently, pretty fun to play in public. Ideally at a cozy coffee shop with squoshy chairs where you can purchase hot London fogs to drink while you play.

Elden Ring was technically playable on the go before the Tarnished Edition , for folks with a Steam Deck. I have one of those, but the device, unlike the Switch 2, is not fun to take out in public. It’s heavy to hold, does not have a convenient kickstand, and you have to hold it in your hands to play if you don’t want to drag a controller around too. With the Switch 2, I could set the console on the table with the kickstand out, take the Joy-Cons off, lean back in my chair, and play Elden Ring while soothing cafe music played in the background. Every time I die (which is often), I get a nice sip of tea. I do not rage. I do not tense up. Helpfully, the cat (who is not here in the cafe with me) does not butt her head against the triggers and cause me to swing my sword randomly. Life is good.

In basically every other respect, I stick to my guns from the preview: this is Elden Ring ! It’s on the Switch 2 now! There were concerns after the first round of early previews that it ran poorly, but those were fixed by the time I previewed it earlier this year and remain fixed now. It runs fine. There are still occasional little framerate drops and yeah, it doesn’t look quite as nice as it will on your PS5 or Xbox Series, but who cares? It still plays great. The minor technical compromises didn’t interfere with combat in any way that was meaningful to me. It still looks good. It’s still lovely to stand on a cliff’s edge and look out in the direction of the Erdtree, the sun’s rays glistening through the clouds and a skyline of crumbling ruin all around.

I should mention that the Tarnished Edition does not have any meaningful new features. There are four new armor sets, a bit of customization for Torrent, and two new starting classes. Unfortunately, two of those new armor sets are starting sets for the two new classes, Heavy Knight and Idus Knight. I played as the Idus Knight and replaced my armor almost immediately with some tunic thing I got off a knight in the very first part of Limgrave, because it had better stats. I think I wore this same tunic when I played the game the first time. Shame, because the new starting armor genuinely looked great. I found the addition of these two new classes to be extremely whatever: you’re going to customize all your stats and replace all your gear almost immediately anyway. The Idus Knight was just a Samurai two levels lower, with different equipment. These additions did nothing for me, and certainly will do nothing for anyone after the first hour of game.

This release does include the superb Shadow of the Erdtree DLC, bundled right in from the start, though. That rules.

But who cares? It’s Elden Ring , on Switch 2! I can easily play it on a plane or on a train, in a box or with a fox, here or there, anywhere! I can take it to bars, to rooftop wine parties. I can play it outside on a patio with a cold one in a koozie next to me as the summer sun sets. I recognize that this is just effectively restating the main gimmick of the Nintendo Switch and Switch 2, but I admittedly haven’t taken my Switch 2 out much since it launched last year. Elden Ring , the best game of 2022 and arguably one of the best games of the decade, is a great excuse to do so. Give it a shot. Order yourself a latte or, a little later in the day, maybe a nice glass of pinot noir, bust out your Switch 2, and give it a shot.

This article was corrected post-publication: Limveld is Nightreign , Limgrave is Elden Ring . I can never keep them straight.

items.title: ELDEN RING - RAGING WOLF 1/6 SCALE STATUE
items.summary: Who is the Raging Wolf? Among the first Tarnished to join the Roundtable Hold was Vargram, a warrior of great skill and ferocity. He acquired the title of the Raging Wolf from the white wolf pelt that flowed from his helm. Vargram sought to
items.content:
Who is the Raging Wolf?

Among the first Tarnished to join the Roundtable Hold was Vargram, a warrior of great skill and ferocity. He acquired the title of the Raging Wolf from the white wolf pelt that flowed from his helm. Vargram sought to become the shadow of one of the Empyreans and built his strength relentlessly as he traveled through fallow Limgrave to the golden city of Leyndell. And yet in spite of all his strength, his armor is now worn by another… An unnamed Tarnished now walks the Lands Between in the skin of the wolf. Does this warrior seek the same fate as Vargram, forever stalking at the side of an Empyrean? Will they uphold the Golden Order or supplant it for some new code? Whatever the destination, woe befall upon any who dare block the path.

The most impressive Elden Ring statue yet

Standing at 33 cm/13 inches, it’s one of the largest character statues ever produced for ELDEN RING. Crafted with the attentive supervision of FromSoftware, this full 1/6 scale figure captures each minute detail with masterful skill. The size allows perfect fidelity to the beautiful and dark fantasy atmosphere of the game, including smears of bloody red across blade of the Bastard Sword and the crest of the Iron Roundshield. From the intricate filigrees of its helm to its whisps of silvered fur blown back by an errant breeze to the humble, dusty cloth wraps protecting the feet of its greaves against the mossy stones of the path to Stoneveil Castle, it’s a portrait of the implacable will of the Tarnished. All these expertly rendered touches from sculpturer Shinya Yamaoka make this statue a perfect match to the most iconic set from one of the most iconic games of this generation.

Where can I get a Raging Wolf Set statue?

Pre-orders for the Raging Wolf 1/6 scale statue can be placed on the official Bandai Namco website. At this time, based on the production estimates of Gecco studio, these stunning PVC/ABS figures will ship to your home in Winter of 2026. If you are a true aficionado of the game, there is no better purchase to bring the world of Elden Ring to your home or office. It’s a timeless piece for your own collection or an impressive gift for a friend or loved one. And one small note, if you have not yet found this set in the Lands Between for your Tarnished, we recommend you seek the aid of Recusant Bernahl at the Volcano Manor.

Place your order for the Raging Wolf statue on the official Bandai Namco Store.

*This product is available on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia, the Middle East, India, and the United States.

items.title: Elden Ring Gets Fun Gameplay Twist In New Free Game Mode
items.summary: Your runes are now a lot more precious in this fun gameplay twist!
items.content:
Your runes are now a lot more precious in this fun gameplay twist.

A new Elden Ring free download has just added a fun gameplay twist to the way you collect runes.

With Elden Ring now being a few years old, players have gotten used to the level of difficulty the game has to offer.

Despite already being a pretty tricky game in itself, some players who desire an extra challenge have gone to extreme lengths to try and make things a little more difficult.

This new mod posted to the Elden Ring Nexus Mods page does exactly that, by putting a fun gameplay twist on the way you collect and deplete runes.

Titled ‘ Action Based Runes ’, the mod adds a rune-based reward and penalty system tied to various gameplay events that can occur while you play.

With the mod installed, you earn runes for damaging enemies, killing them while at low health, and picking up or crafting items. Meanwhile, you will also lose runes if you take damage or die.

Essentially, it adds a new risk/reward system to the game where you’ll earn loads of runes if you play well, but run the risk of losing more if you play sloppily or get unlucky.

If you do find it a little unfair though (or alternatively, not unfair enough), the mod also has a built-in tool to be able to configure it to your liking. So, feel free to go nuts with it.

It’s a little similar to another mod I covered a few weeks ago, Rune Health , which changed the value of your health depending on how many runes you’re holding.

Combining both mods might seem like a recipe for disaster, but it also might give you the extra hard difficulty mode that you know you’re craving. Use at your own risk.

Altogether though, it proves just how tantalising the Elden Ring experience is, that a game already known for being quite challenging is evoking more players to seek out harder challenges.

In other Elden Ring news, the upcoming movie produced by A24 has started principal photography. Directed by Alex Garland, the film stars Kit Connor, Cailee Spaeny, Ben Whishaw, Nick Offerman, Tom Burke, Jonathan Pryce, and Peter Serafinowicz.

It’s currently filming in the United Kingdom and Scotland, with further filming occurring in Iceland over the summer. Filming is expected to last 100 days, and a lengthy post-production schedule is expected following that.

items.title: I'm obsessed with a guy who keeps soloing Elden Ring Nightreign's hard mode over and over like they're trapped in a purgatory of their own making

(Image credit: FromSoftware) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Facebook X Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 3 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter We all have our guys, the true freaks and sickos online who it feels like only we know about, whose trials and travails move us in ways we can scarcely explain. Replica sword reviewers, world-class competitors in niche sports, historical reenactors with hearts of gold⁠—you know, your guys . One such guy, for me, is eauvni , a YouTuber who silently and implacably keeps playing Elden Ring Nightreign alone, then uploading the VODs.

Crucially, eauvni is very good at Elden Ring Nightreign, and will upload multiple runs a week, like clockwork. They rotate through the entire cast, but seem to have a particular affinity for the Sekiro-parrying Executor. All of their runs have been in the mega-hard Deep of Night mode since its release at the end of last year, but they've exclusively uploaded VODs of Depth Three of Five in recent months.

Watch On My guess would be that, even at this skill level, solo Depth Five just isn't fun⁠—even Sekiro/Souls no-hit maestro Ongbal has said as much (in the description of a successful Depth Five solo run , naturally). My understanding is that the jump in difficulty from Depth Three to Four is the most pronounced in the game, with enemies dealing twice as much damage in Four vs. Three⁠—and that's on top of the three depths worth of DoN advancements over the base game already.

The Depth Three/Four barrier is what separates the freaks from the perverts among Nightreign players, while the Four/Five divide splits the perverts and the reprobates.

The individual videos are prime "have something on in the background while you do something else" material for me, but as a whole, eauvni's body of work is kind of staggering as a record of obsession: Dozens and dozens of Nightreign runs, all on the same two maps with the same bosses. I've played a fraction as much of this game as eauvni, and there's a point where you start to see the Matrix code, you recognize different map seeds and can even anticipate individual boss placements.

Elden Ring's Tarnished Edition is exciting enough on its own, but it's also our last chance to properly experience the game's launch day hype Elden Ring players are hard at work putting the new Tarnished Edition DLC's gear to the test The most deranged videogame challenge run I've seen: A no-hit playthrough of the 'Unfair' difficulty in a 100-hour RPG Full Run No Damage - Executor | Deep of Night - YouTube Watch On And all to seemingly no end: Eauvni has reached Depth Five and turned back, content to keep fighting more manageable versions of the same pool of base Elden Ring bosses. They already have mathematically perfect relic builds for every character. There is, seemingly, no further support or content for the game planned in the future, nothing to anticipate or prepare for. Alexander wept, for there were no more worlds to conquer.

I can relate to this obession, even at a much lower skill level: Almost every day for our lunch break, PCG writers Tyler Colp, Sean Martin, and I do a Nightreign run. We are in the latter half of Depth Four, coming up on Depth Five, and I have never felt more hated by a game.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Eauvni's " Thank You Nightreign Compilation " is very illustrative: Even more than FromSoft's other games, whether it's glitches, enemy AI, or RNG odds, there's a spite lurking beneath Nightreign. It feels like there's a malicious intelligence working against you at all times. This only makes eauvni's stoic, meditative repetition all the more disquieting to me.

Their recent no-damage run as Executor is a real heater: Eauvni has a habit of level one bum rushing bosses I'd be hesitant to tango with at the end of a run. They began this latest video with a ballsy, flawlessly executed level two takedown of a red (read: turbocharged) Erdtree Avatar at the top of Limveld castle. Elsewhere, they've 1v1'd the memetically difficult Bell Bearing Hunter at level one so many times, it almost doesn't feel worth commenting on anymore.

My friends and I aren't as good as eauvni, but part of me is worried that Nightreign will ruin normal FromSoft games for us and other disturbed Deep of Night holdouts: When I finally replay Elden Ring again with the Tarnished Edition patch allegedly due out this year, will it just feel too fair and well-balanced for me to enjoy? When I'm not instakilled by an overtuned area of effect attack in FromSoft's next mainline release, will I miss the thrill?

items.title: ELDEN RING: SHADOW OF THE ERDTREE – Official Vinyl Soundtrack
items.summary: Follow in the foosteps of Miquella once more with this exclusive 2 disc vinyl collection, celebrating the sweeping, emotional journey of Shadow of the Erdtree. Presented with the reverence merited by a legendary expansion, this premium set
items.content:
Follow in the foosteps of Miquella once more with this exclusive 2 disc vinyl collection, celebrating the sweeping, emotional journey of Shadow of the Erdtree.

Presented with the reverence merited by a legendary expansion, this premium set is crafted for collectors, audiophiles, and Tarnished who seek to experience the Realm of Shadow through its music.

The Collection

Housed in a full color gatefold sleeve and marked with the symbol of Messmer the Impaler, each vinyl disc is pressed on heavyweight material to ensure optimal durability and warmth of playback. Whether displayed proudly on a shelf or played to relive your own quest, this set is designed as both a collector’s piece and a lasting tribute to one of the most celebrated expansions in modern gaming.

The Artists

Across 18 tracks, the soundtrack transforms the ELDEN RING experience into a powerful standalone odyssey—one carried by orchestral grandeur, ethereal choir work, and the signature melancholy that defines the worlds created by FromSoftware.

A Collector’s Treasure

This official vinyl set is an essential centerpiece for any discerning fan’s collection. Perfect for longtime followers of FromSoftware’s musical legacy or newcomers drawn into the Land of Shadow for the first time. *This vinyl is available exclusively on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia, Middle East, India and the United States

items.title: Discover the ELDEN RING Blaidd The Half-Wolf Lamp
items.summary: Summon the legendary warrior into your world with the Blaidd The Half-Wolf Lamp, a handcrafted, LED-powered tribute to one of ELDEN RING ’s most iconic character. Designed for collectors, lore enthusiasts, and Tarnished alike, this unique n
items.content:
Summon the legendary warrior into your world with the Blaidd The Half-Wolf Lamp, a handcrafted, LED-powered tribute to one of ELDEN RING’s most iconic character.

Designed for collectors, lore enthusiasts, and Tarnished alike, this unique night lamp captures the tragic loyalty and silent strength of Blaidd, Shadow of Ranni.

The lamp features an LED-illuminated base that reveals glowing rune symbols beneath Blaidd’s feet, evoking the grace-given power that guides Tarnished across the Lands Between. Rising above it, an engraved acrylic summoning panel glows softly when lit, capturing the look and feel of an in-game summon sign and the spirit-calling magic it represents. Powered through a simple USB connection, it offers effortless illumination for any desk, gaming setup, or collector’s display.

"If ever thou shouldst call upon me… I shall come."

Blaidd’s oath echoes still. Now, he stands ready, not for battle, but as a silent guardian of your space.

Bring the moonlit magic of ELDEN RING into your world, one glowing rune at a time.

*This edition is available exclusively on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia and the United States.

items.content:
Facebook Threads Discord TikTok Instagram X Home Comics Blog Gaming Shop Patreon Discord SCORE 8.5/10 Elden Ring: Nightreign – review January 9, 2026 written by

Like many gamers, I’ve been playing FromSoftware stuff for a long time now, dating all the way back to Demon’s Souls on PS3 over 15 years ago. When Elden Ring came on the scene back in 2022, it was a very solid culmination of years of refinement of Miyazaki’s “souls” formula brought to a new(ish) IP to great success.

When Nightreign was first announced, I was skeptical about the entire idea of a Fortnite-inspired Elden Ring spin-off. I mean, I actually thought it was just a DLC until it actually came out. However, after nearly 100 hours on the game, I can faithfully say that Nightreign has become a new favorite of mine for its addictive gameplay loop and fast-paced action.

Fast-paced is the keyword here. From the moment you load into the map, you have what feels like mere moments to accomplish everything you need to accomplish. The basic idea of the game is Elden Ring gameplay and vibes, but with a Fortnite-inspired toxic ring that slowly shuts down the map every few minutes and funnels you toward the boss fight. Starting at level 1 every time, you have this limited amount of time to gain as many levels as possible (maxing at 15), collect as many weapons and buffs as you can, and face the boss with up to 2 of your best friends (or random players–or solo).

Writing this out, it doesn’t sound fun, but it ends up being a frenetic and extremely engaging time where you’re absolutely locked in for every moment. This is ultimately what makes the game so addicting, and you can expect each match to last about 45 minutes from start to finish (if you make it to the end “Nightlord” boss).

Replacing the iconic character creator from Elden Ring is a selection of 8 set characters with unique classes and abilities (plus 2 more if you get the recently released DLC). Each character fills a specific role:

Wylder is a kind of standard warrior type with a small shield and big sword, Recluse is a wizard with a big hat, Guardian (my favorite) is a defensive role with a big shield and a halberd, etc.

Initially I was disappointed at the lack of a customizable character creator, but the game is designed to be fast, simple and broad enough to accommodate the game loop. I do think it would be nice if each archetype class had an ability to customize the character, but at the very least, you can unlock a number of different skins for each one.

My biggest complaint about the game is the relic system, which is basically a gacha gambling roll for a stone that you can equip that gives you some stat-bonuses. The issue with it is that, with 10 characters in the game, you often get stones that are completely irrelevant to you, and there’s very seriously no way to influence what stones you get. Each run through the game rewards you with a handful of them, and they are 100% random. It would be nice to have some kind of crafting system where you can at least combine certain effects to make new stones that you can actually use. As it is right now, the system is more frustrating than anything else.

But that’s a minor gripe to an otherwise strangely addicting Elden Ring romp. It might seem like “SlopSouls,” but Nightreign has weirdly been one of my favorite games of the last year.
